::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** January 10, 1872.  
**From:** Palace, Lichfield,  
**Manuscript:** MS location unknown.  Printed in Coleridge, [<i>Life</i>](other_books/otherbook_40.qmd), 300-301
:::

My dear [Sir William](people/person_669.qmd)-
Your letter has come on to me here. I came on Monday to be instructed respecting[Bishop Patteson](people/person_1155.qmd)'s life, which I am to try to [draw up](cmy_books/cmybook_102.qmd) from the very full materials that his family and [Bishop Selwyn](people/person_1295.qmd) can provide. I hope to return on Saturday.

Thank you for letting me see [Mr. Faithfull](people/person_497.qmd)'s decision; I think he is wise to give his name, and so obtain the subscriptions of all his friends. I daresay in this way he will obtain a good

deal of pleasure out of it himself, and I hope some benefit to the hospital funds.-[^1]

Your affectionate
C. M. YONGE.

---

[^1]: Edward Williams Faithfull, *Occasional Thoughts* (London, E. Faithfull, and Winchester, Jacob and Johnson  1872), a volume of verse published by private subscription, probably in aid of the rebuilt [Royal Hampshire Hospital](organizations/other_36.qmd) in Winchester.
